No exact published comparison of learned depth aggregation versus uniform averaging, final-block readout, and parameter-matched projections was located. Closest recommendation evidence: SkipRec jointly trains a NextItNet backbone and layer-skipping policy; compares learned policies against Bernoulli(0.5) random skipping, CNN versus GRU policy networks, and training with/without backbone pretraining. It uses LayerNorm, zero-initialized residual coefficients, and Gumbel-softmax temperature 10. Diagnostics show average block utilization, rather than gate entropy or explicit collapse tests. Reported inference speedups reach 2.30×; peak GPU memory and isolated gate parameter overhead are not reported. This studies skipping, not weighted depth readout. [SkipRec](https://cdn.aaai.org/ojs/16518/16518-13-20012-1-2-20210518.pdf)

Relevant multiscale evidence comes from vision: Selective Kernel Networks compare softmax-gated branches against simple branch summation—not uniform averaging—and approximately match capacity using wider/deeper/higher-cardinality baselines. Two-branch gating reduces ImageNet top-1 error from 21.76% to 20.79%, while parameters rise from 26.5M to 27.5M and computation from 4.46 to 4.47 GFLOPs. Uses He initialization, BatchNorm/ReLU, bottleneck gate projections; diagnostics visualize attention means and standard deviations across input scales. These findings do not establish results for causal recommendation. [SKNet](https://arxiv.org/html/1903.06586)

Suggested controls, not reported findings: identical NextItNet backbone with learned gates, fixed 1/K weights, final-block readout, and a comparably sized projection head. Initialize gate logits to zero; normalize representations consistently. Measure gate entropy, saturation, per-depth usage and variation across users/history lengths; report added parameters, training time, and peak allocated GPU memory at identical batch size, sequence length and precision. Neither source supplies the requested complete control suite or GPU-memory comparison.
